title: Horizontal Compression of a Parabola
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Give an equation for the graph of y = x^2 - 1 after it is compressed horizontally by a factor of 2.

steps.title: Recall the Horizontal Compression Rule
steps.explanation: To compress the graph of y = f(x) horizontally toward the y-axis by a factor of c > 1, replace x with c*x.
steps.why: Replacing x with c*x divides every x-coordinate on the graph by c.

steps.title: Substitute 2x for x
steps.explanation: With compression factor c = 2, replace x in y = x^2 - 1 with 2x.
steps.why: Horizontal compression by a factor of 2 replaces x with 2x.

steps.title: Simplify the Squared Term
steps.explanation: Squaring 2x gives 4x^2, so the compressed graph has equation y = 4x^2 - 1 (with x-intercepts compressed from (+/-1, 0) to (+/-1/2, 0)).
